text:
maria: Hey team, seeing a spike in scheduling failures for the `us-west1-mgpu` nodepool since the rollout. Lots of `Pending` pods. kubectl describe shows:

maria: ```
Events:
  Type     Reason            Age   From               Message
  ----     ------            ----  ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling  2m    default-scheduler  0/24 nodes are available: 18 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 6 node(s) had taint {dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule}.
```

maria: This cluster has a mix of A100 and T4 nodes in the same pool and some nodes are labeled `gpu-type=a100` vs `gpu-type=t4`. Pods request `resources.requests: nvidia.com/gpu: 1` (generic). Not sure why the scheduler can't binpack them.

kai: ugh, mixed-GPU pools + taints = classic fragmentation. A100 nodes advertise `nvidia.com/gpu` too but we changed device-plugin config to expose `nvidia.com/gpu-a100` on some pools last month for telemetry. If pods request generic `nvidia.com/gpu` they might not bind to the a100-specific resource.

devon: Also the taint `dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule` is applied only on A100 nodes so non-tolerating pods can't land there — that's why Insufficient appears even though capacity exists. We intentionally tainted A100 for latency-sensitive jobs, but the autoscaler is scaling T4 nodes for cheaper throughput which increases fragmentation.

samir: cost angle: A100s are 6x T4 cost. Right now cheaper T4 nodes are being scaled up because preemptible/pool config triggers first. That leaves expensive A100s underutilized but reserved.

oncall-bot: Pending pods (last 5):
- core-train-77b (requests: `nvidia.com/gpu:1`, priorityClass: high)
- batch-rerank-3 (requests: `nvidia.com/gpu:1`, priorityClass: default)
- explore-ctl-2 (requests: `nvidia.com/gpu:2`, nodeAffinity: `gpu-type=a100`)

maria: I pushed a quick `kubectl get nodes -L gpu-type,dedicated | sort -k3` and saw 12 nodes labeled `t4` scaled to 0 recently, and 6 `a100` nodes still cordoned/tainted.

kai: Proposed quick fixes:
- If we want generic scheduling, revert device-plugin naming so all nodes advertise `nvidia.com/gpu` (short-term).
- Or change our pod specs to include `nodeAffinity` for `gpu-type` and update autoscaler profiles to scale matching machine type.
- Add a toleration for `dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule` on the latency-sensitive pods (they already have it) and add toleration to some batch jobs if safe.

devon: Long-term: split nodepools by GPU type (no mixing), have pool-level autoscaler config, and use the cluster-autoscaler expander policy `least-waste` with proper resourceBalance. Also consider `--balance-similar-node-groups` off for now, it's interacting badly with mixed types.

samir: We should also evaluate using node-level packing: add a `binpack` topologySpread/affinity policy to concentrate small GPU jobs onto T4s and reserve A100 for larger requests (>=4 gpus) to reduce fragmentation.

maria: Quick attempt in prod: adding toleration to batch-rerank-3 and a temporary podAffinity to prefer `gpu-type=t4`. Will watch.

sre-bot: FYI cluster autoscaler recently patched v1.22.1 -> v1.23.2 on staging two days ago. Patch notes mention resource name changes for device plugins. Might be relevant. Link: https://git.internal/release/ca-1.23.2

kai: We should do a 30m incident window: action items:
- [maria] revert device-plugin name change in dev first and run scheduler sim w/ test pods.
- [devon] create a separate nodepool spec for `a100-dedicated` and set taint/toleration strategy.
- [samir] run a cost tradeoff projection if we consolidate to separate pools (expected +$12k/mo).
- [sre-bot] check if autoscaler expander config drifted from desired.

maria: Sounds good. If anyone sees pods stuck >10m ping me and I'll evict tests. :thumbsup:

kai: Also note: if we change resource name, we need to update Helm charts for runtime deployments to request `nvidia.com/gpu-a100` vs `nvidia.com/gpu-t4` explicitly.

devon: temp workaround: taint some T4 nodes with `dedicated=gpu:PreferNoSchedule` instead of `NoSchedule` to allow priority pods to fill A100s when needed. Not ideal but helpful for immediate relief.

maria: I'll coordinate the revert in dev and post results here. Thanks all.

samir: tagging cost team for visibility: @finance (just FYI).

oncall-bot: Incident window opened by kai at 1780213400.

maria: updating status: after adding toleration to the batch job and forcing a scale-up of a small T4 pool, 4 of the pending pods moved to Running. Still 2 big ones waiting on A100.

kai: good progress. We should schedule a follow-up doc for nodepool design and autoscaler profiles.

devon: noted — I'll draft a runbook item for mixed-gpu pitfalls and add a checklist: device-plugin names, taints, autoscaler profile, pod resource name.

maria: closing the quick incident when remaining pods start or hit 30m.

maria: ```
Action: revert device-plugin naming in dev -> test -> prod
Owner: maria
ETA: 6h (dev), 24h (prod)
```
